Fusebox follows Claude's new plans: Max 20x is now Ultra and Max 5x is Max, and verified Ultra accounts have no 5-hour limit. Signing in again repairs the account you already have instead of adding a second one, and usage costs now follow T3 Code's pricing.

## Changes

- **Claude Ultra and Max.** Anthropic renamed its plans on 30 October 2026. Accounts show the plan name Claude gives them (Ultra, Max, Pro), and older profiles fall back from the unchanged `max_20x` and `max_5x` identifiers. Combined weekly limits still weigh Pro 1, Max 5 and Ultra 10, which are now Anthropic's published weekly allowances.
- **No 5-hour limit on verified Ultra.** When usage confirms it (`five_hour: null` with a typed limit list that has a weekly entry and no session), Fusebox retires the account's old 5-hour window, the cooldown it caused and its attribution, and the 5H meter reads **No limit**. Unverified Ultra accounts keep their temporary limit and are followed as before, and a 5-hour window that comes back restores the limit. Missing, malformed or ambiguous data never removes a limit.
- **Window starter.** Accounts without a 5-hour limit get no starter requests and show that there is no window to start. They are rechecked hourly, or within five minutes once a 5-hour window is reported again. An active session in the typed list is never taken for an idle window, and on Ultra a bare null only gets a status check.
- **Pace warnings and banked resets.** There is no combined 5-hour pace warning while an Ultra account that is signed in, not paused and has weekly quota left can take the overflow. Automatic banked resets skip a grant that only clears a 5-hour limit the account no longer has.
- **Signing in again.** A new sign-in for an account Fusebox already has is saved into that account's credential file, whatever its name (older releases wrote names like `claude-<hash>-<email>.json`). The account keeps its ID, priority, window-starter selection and sessions, and no stale copy keeps retrying a revoked refresh token. The new tokens take effect at once, even while a refresh of the old ones is running, and an error from the old sign-in such as `invalid_grant` clears. Every Claude and ChatGPT sign-in then reads its usage and plan straight away.
- **Usage pricing.** The default rate catalogue is `t3-2026-10-30.1`, compiled from the LiteLLM rates T3 Code caches and using T3 Code's cost categories. Codex calls are priced at the speed they requested. Streams keep the usage already received when a client disconnects, and the dashboard's coverage separates missing usage from missing prices.

## Upgrading

- The usage database stays on schema 5. The first start adds one index; there are no new settings.
- Existing cost estimates stay as they are unless you run `fusebox usage reprice --all`. Older usage priced from the new catalogue is labelled `t3_current_rate_equivalent`.
- `/api/accounts` adds `quota.plan_name` and `quota.no_five_hour_limit`, and the window starter can report `not_needed`. Plan identifiers are unchanged.
- If an earlier sign-in left a second copy of an account that keeps failing with `invalid_grant`, remove that copy; signing in again no longer creates one.

Validation passed 782 Rust, 149 dashboard and 46 Python tests, plus release candidate, restart and rollback checks. The [research](https://github.com/DigitalPals/Fusebox/blob/v0.12.0/notes/anthropic-max-ultra-research-2026-10-31.md) and two reviews ([first](https://github.com/DigitalPals/Fusebox/blob/v0.12.0/notes/anthropic-max-ultra-implementation-review-2026-10-31.md), [follow-up](https://github.com/DigitalPals/Fusebox/blob/v0.12.0/notes/anthropic-max-ultra-followup-review-2026-10-31.md)) behind the Ultra changes are in the repository.

[Full comparison with v0.11.1](https://github.com/DigitalPals/Fusebox/compare/v0.11.1...v0.12.0).
